title: PIC S9(n) without SIGN clause — sign embedded in the last digit's high nibble (overpunch)
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SIGN-VARIANTS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> WS-AMT-1 stores sign in the last byte's high nibble
      *>   ('overpunch'): '5' = 0xF5 positive, 'N' = 0xD5 negative.
      *> WS-AMT-2 stores sign as a SEPARATE character before or
      *>   after the digits. Reading raw bytes assumes one or the
      *>   other -- and silently produces garbage on the wrong
      *>   guess.
       01  WS-AMT-1    PIC S9(5)V99.
       01  WS-AMT-2    PIC S9(5)V99 SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           STOP RUN.
notes: Sign storage variations are notoriously hard to spot on a code review. The same PIC S9(5)V99 produces 7 bytes (no SIGN clause), 7 bytes (LEADING/TRAILING SEPARATE adds a separate byte), depending on the clause. The spec must capture which variant is in use AND surface the byte-layout question.
